hypothesis: On a predefined family of deterministic optimization tasks, a feedback-driven adaptive search policy improves held-out task performance over a fixed-policy baseline under a matched evaluation budget. Improvement must appear on previously unseen test instances (seeds 1000-1015) that neither method saw during adaptation, ruling out simple memorization of training instances.
notes: PREREGISTERED before any held-out evaluation. Matched budget: both methods receive exactly 60 objective evaluations per instance. Candidate modifications are restricted to the declared action_bounds; the evaluator, baseline, seeds, budget, and acceptance policy are outside the candidate's modification surface. Score scales: quadratic losses and rastrigin losses are O(10-100) on these difficulty settings, so the primary acceptance margin of 1.0 is a small but non-trivial practical threshold. Decisions recorded before evaluation: 16 held-out test instances per task family; bootstrap 5000 resamples; exact sign-flip permutation test (n_pairs=32 > 14 -> Monte Carlo with 20000 draws, seeded).
